basis: Power Integrations’ November 2 release establishes that Q3 2022 consolidated GAAP net revenue was $160,233,000, down 9.36% from $176,776,000 in Q3 2021 and below the $167,937,200 cutoff. August 4 guidance had a $173,250,000 high end. The earliest public date remains unresolved because the full August 31 Deutsche Bank fireside chat could not be verified. The September Analyst Day transcript refers back to the August guidance but does not establish everything the CFO said on August 31.

coverage.detail: April 28 Q1 earnings release. The $190 million ± $5 million forecast explicitly covered Q2 2022.
April 28 earnings Q&A. The CEO said management needed to see Q2 distributor sell-through to assess Q3 and Q4. He gave no numeric Q3 revenue ceiling.

The issuer’s May 27 notice identifies two additional preceding-cycle webcasts: Cowen on June 2 and Stifel on June 7. The notice gives times and directs listeners to issuer IR. Searches recovered the notice but neither full set of remarks.
August 4 Q2 earnings release. The explicit Q3 revenue forecast was $165 million ± 5%, or $156,750,000–$173,250,000. Its high end exceeded the cutoff by $5,312,800.

August 4 earnings call, secondary transcript check. The CFO repeated the September-quarter range and said backlog coverage was within it. In Q&A he said the estimate could move either way. The SEC exhibit above supplies the primary guidance.

August 26 issuer notice. CFO Sandeep Nayyar was scheduled to speak publicly on August 31 at 4:30 p.m. Pacific. The notice points to the IR homepage and contains no financial forecast or session-specific replay link.
Deutsche Bank’s original schedule independently places Nayyar in Session C, Chopin 4, from 4:30 to 5:05 p.m. Pacific on August 31. It establishes the precise session but contains no remarks.
The host’s 2022 archive lists the Las Vegas Technology Conference. Its event link leads to the reused registration page below.
The event link now displays the 2026 Dana Point conference. It yielded no 2022 Power Integrations audio, slides or transcript.
The issuer’s accessible archive page showed a presentation-year selector but exposed no August 31 recording, deck or transcript.
The historical index query for the issuer’s 2022 events pages was inaccessible. Whether a snapshot preserves the original webcast link remains unknown.

The searchable secondary excerpt identifies Nayyar and IR director Joe Shiffler and shows the moderator’s opening channel-inventory question. Direct retrieval did not expose the full Q&A. The excerpt cannot resolve whether management narrowed guidance.
The issuer’s Analyst Day agenda dates the public event to September 8, including Nayyar’s financial presentation and a subsequent Q&A. The transcript header reads September 9.

Analyst Day Q&A, page 39. Asked what had changed since earnings, Nayyar referred back to the $165 million range and discussed waiting for sell-through. His expectation of a sequential decline concerned Q4. He gave no tighter numeric Q3 ceiling.
The October 11 issuer scheduling notice, preserved by a distributor, announced November 2 results and call timing. It supplied no preliminary revenue figure.
October 28 Form 8-K. Item 5.02 reported director Jennifer Lloyd’s October 25 resignation. It contained no revenue update.

November 2 actuals. The consolidated income statement reports net revenues in thousands of $160,233 and $176,776 in the respective September 2022 and September 2021 three-month columns. The $125 million ± $5 million outlook applied to Q4.

publication_date_evidence: Exhibit 99.1 carries the issuer’s November 2, 2022 Business Wire dateline and announces results for the quarter ended September 30. That verifies the public date and exact amount of the qualifying actuals. The incomplete August 31 record prevents certifying November 2 as the first qualifying disclosure.
